feat(core+cli+mcp): S+2 — signal transport + flyway_check

ADR-0008 (Proposed) settles the on-disk shape of cross-murmuration
signals before any senders exist, so the senders drop in without
changing what receivers expect:

  envelope    SignalEnvelope { schema, id, from, to, sentAt, kind, body, refs? }
              signed inline under DOMAIN_TENSION / _PROPOSAL / _RESPOND / _EXIT
              (kind-specific so signatures cannot be cross-kind replayed)
  location    flyway/inbox/<host>/<owner>/<repo>/<id>.yaml   (recipient)
              flyway/outbox/<host>/<owner>/<repo>/<id>.yaml  (sender)
              ids: <unix-ms-13>-<8-hex>, time-sortable, charset-bounded
  transport   pluggable; v0.1 ships local-fs (direct write into peer's
              repo); github-pr and url-webhook reserved for later ADRs

Implementation (flyway-core):
  signal.ts   types, domainForSignalKind, buildSignedSignal,
              verifySignedSignal, generateSignalId, writeSignalToInbox/Outbox
              (idempotent; refuses overwrite with different signature)
  check.ts   flywayCheck(cwd) walks flyway/inbox/, parses each envelope,
              verifies envelope.from is in peers.yaml, loads cached peer
              DID document, verifies signature under the kind-derived
              domain, reports per-signal validity + issues

Wiring:
  MCP        flyway_check handler — accepts optional cwd, defaults to
              process.cwd()
  CLI        `flyway check [--json]` — non-zero exit if any signal fails
              to verify

Tests: 166 passing (+13 core signal, +5 core check). End-to-end smoke
verified: A sends a tension to B (recognized, sig valid); C sends a
proposal to B without recognition (unverified, clear "not in
flyway/peers.yaml" issue).

ADR-0008 left as Proposed pending Source review.

fix(core+cli): close the three Tier 1 walkthrough gaps

G1 — Peer public key inline in recognition entries
  RecognitionEntry gains peerVerificationKeyId + peerPublicKey, populated
  from the peer's DID document at recognition time. The peer's key
  becomes part of the signed payload, so future peer key rotation is
  detectable from the entry alone (no DID document re-fetch required).

G2 — flyway unrecognize verb
  New core primitive unrecognizePeer() produces a signed
  UnrecognitionRecord under DOMAIN_UNRECOGNITION = 'flyway-v1:unrecognition'.
  Only the original recognizer may unrecognize (signer DID must match
  priorEntry.recognizedBy). CLI exposes `flyway unrecognize <did>
  [--reason "..."]`: writes the signed record to
  flyway/unrecognized/<safe-did>.yaml, removes the peer from
  flyway/peers.yaml, and intentionally retains the peer cache for audit.

G3 — Peer identity drift detection in flyway_status
  Status now reads each peer's cached did.json + entity-statement.json and
  compares against the recognition entry's bindings:
    - peerPublicKey vs. cached DID document's verification method  → key rotation
    - entityStatementFingerprint vs. re-hashed cached statement     → statement reissue
  Reports per-peer cacheConsistent + issues array. Legacy entries without
  inline peerPublicKey are tolerated with a "rerun recognize" hint.

Tests: 148 passing (+2 core recognize G1/G2, +2 core status G3 drift
scenarios, +7 CLI unrecognize). End-to-end smoke verified: recognize →
peers.yaml shows inline key → unrecognize → audit record written →
peers.yaml empty.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

docs(walkthroughs): Tier 1 mutual recognition — first executable walkthrough

End-to-end walkthrough of flyway_init + flyway_recognize + flyway_status
against real on-disk artifacts. Two murmurations create their identities,
verify each other's signed entity statements, and produce signed
recognition entries — each step reproducible from SHA 1712232.

Distinct from the 2026-05-13 narrative walkthrough: the actors here are
real CLI invocations, the evidence is files on disk, and the signatures
round-trip through cryptographic verify. Updated walkthroughs/README to
distinguish narrative vs. executable kinds.

Surfaces three new gaps worth filing (peer public key not in peers.yaml;
no flyway_unrecognize; peer identity drift not detected).

* Preserve metrics, visualization, and answer generation flows
